title: Interview syllabus tracker
ready: Ready = you can explain it aloud in a minute, solve a small case on it and answer one follow-up.
order: Prepare your domain and Core first, then your second choice.

topics.know: 45 seconds: name and city, how you cleared Inter, one thing beyond the books, why this domain. Family in one line at the end, or leave it out.
Exact months and groups, said plainly. More than one attempt: the true count in one line and what you changed.

topics.topic: Why CA, this firm, this domain
topics.know: Three answers tied to the real work of the team you applied to, never to the firm's size or brand.

read.find: Why do you want to join us

topics.know: Two strengths, each with a small proof. One real weakness and what you are doing about it; never perfectionism.
Each line is a question: what you did, how many, what you found, what you learnt. Work Simulation lines too.
Qualified, good at this domain's work, trusted with bigger tasks. Talk about learning, not titles.
Never raise it. If asked: a later decision you would take with your principal's consent; right now you want to learn the work here.

topics.topic: A difficult situation, a team task
topics.know: Two true stories: the situation, what you did, the result. College, exams, a family business or a project all count.
A client delays documents, a voucher looks fake, your senior disagrees, you find your own error: your first step and who you tell.
Your real earliest joining date, ICITSS status exactly as it is, travel only if true, any CS or CMA said honestly.
Phone on ring, answer unknown numbers, note the caller, firm and next step. Attempts, joining date and cities ready.
The team you applied to, what it does, its clients' sectors from the firm's own site, one recent news item, your 'why this team' line.
If your firm has a page: how it hires and what students were asked there. Answer each question aloud once.
Two about the work: what an article in this team does first, how work is reviewed. Hours and policies go to current articles, or HR after the offer.
Say so in one line, say how you would find out, then bridge to what you do know. Never guess a section number.
Say them aloud with numbers: a sale with GST, fees with TDS, prepaid insurance, outstanding salary, a customer advance, a bad debt.
Lower of cost and NRV, item by item; what goes into cost; FIFO and weighted average; the disclosures.
When revenue is recognised for goods, services, interest and dividends, and what to do when collection is uncertain.
What goes into cost, capital or revenue spend, when depreciation starts, and the disclosures.
Two more you can explain fully, with an example and their disclosures. 'Your favourite AS' always gets a follow-up.
AS 1, 4, 12, 16, 22, 26 and 29: what each covers and one example. Provision vs contingent liability comes up often.
Who follows Ind AS, one difference you can explain, and Ind AS 115's five steps in outline.
Follow one change, such as extra depreciation, through the profit and loss, the balance sheet and the cash flow.
Classify common items as operating, investing or financing, and say why a profitable company can run short of cash.
Current, quick, debt-equity, interest cover, ROCE, ROE, debtor days: compute one and say what it tells you.
Main headings of the balance sheet and profit and loss, current vs non-current, and where common items sit.
What a tallied trial balance does not prove, and why the bank balance differs from the books and how each item clears.
MoA vs AoA, separate legal entity, limited liability, who approves the accounts, related-party approvals in outline.
Contribution and break-even, NPV and IRR, working capital, operating vs financial leverage.
Acceptance, planning, risk assessment, fieldwork, completion and reporting, with one task an article does at each stage.
Existence, completeness, accuracy, cut-off, classification, rights and obligations, and the direction of testing for each.
Overall, performance and clearly trivial; how a benchmark is chosen; why performance materiality is lower.
Tests of controls vs substantive tests, vouching vs tracing, confirmations, analytical procedures.
Unmodified, qualified, adverse and disclaimer, when each is given; emphasis of matter vs other matter.
The common SAs by number and purpose: 200, 230, 240, 300, 315, 320, 330, 500, 530, 570, 580 and 700.
What CARO is, that it is reported alongside the audit opinion, and two clauses you can explain: inventory and statutory dues.
Classify the payment first, then threshold and rate. Most non-salary TDS falls due on credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
Who deducts or collects, from whom, and one example of each.
The Income-tax Act, 2025 from tax year 2026–27; earlier years stay under the 1961 Act. Ask which year a question is about.
The conditions to claim it, blocked credit with two examples, and why the books and GSTR-2B can differ.
Who pays the tax, the common cases, the entry, and when the credit can be taken.
VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP and INDEX-MATCH with exact match, and what you do with missing or duplicate keys.
Conditional totals that tie back to the source; SUBTOTAL vs SUM on a filtered list.
Build, refresh and filter one, and say what you would use it for in an audit.
TRIM, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, TEXT and date fixes: a clean key before any lookup.
Simple logic, and IFERROR only where an error is expected, never to hide a real one.
Raw data to one PivotTable to one insight, timed. Some firms give a live task while you share your screen.
Ctrl+T table, Ctrl+Shift+L filter, Alt+= sum, F4 to fix a reference, Ctrl+arrow to jump. Use them while sharing your screen.
The five-stage answer, with what an article does at each stage and one example.
What you ask for: trial balance, ledgers, last year's file, bank statements, fixed-asset register, stock records.
Occurrence and cut-off for sales; confirmations and later receipts for debtors; what if a debtor doesn't reply.
Attending the count, test counts both ways, valuation at lower of cost and NRV, slow-moving items.
Additions vouched, capitalisation date, depreciation recomputed, physical verification, capital items booked as repairs.
Reconciliation items traced to the next statement; why a confirmation must come straight to the auditor.
Vouch against PO, GRN and invoice; search for unrecorded liabilities; find ghost employees.
Test the last and first entries around year end. Vouching proves an entry; verification proves an asset exists.
Subsequent events, going concern, written representations, and what happens to misstatements you found.
The CARO checks on inventory, fixed assets and statutory dues, and what IFC reporting asks of the auditor.
Enquiry and analytics instead of full testing, so the conclusion says nothing has come to the auditor's attention.

topics.topic: Auditor rules in the Companies Act
topics.know: Appointment and removal (s.139, 140), who can't be an auditor (s.141), barred services (s.144), fraud reporting (s.143(12)).
Who appoints, whom it reports to, its scope, and what each one produces.
Explain any process this way, with purchasing as your example, and look for the root cause.
Its columns, and how a process narrative and a walkthrough fill it.
The steps, the risks (fake vendors, duplicate payments, no approval) and the controls, three-way match included.
Credit limits, dispatch, invoicing, collection and credit notes: the risks and the controls.
Joiners, leavers, attendance and salary changes: the risks and the controls.
Maker-checker, incompatible access and compensating controls, each with an example.
Design vs operating effectiveness, sample, evidence and exceptions; manual vs automated controls.
What each means, who reports on them, and IT general controls in outline.
Condition, criteria, root cause, impact, recommendation, owner and date, with one worked example.
The Income-tax Act, 2025 from tax year 2026–27. FY 2025–26 and earlier stay under the 1961 Act, even when filed later.

topics.topic: What an article does in tax
topics.know: Computations and returns, TDS deposits and quarterly returns, advance tax, AIS matching, tax-audit schedules, notice replies.
The five heads, and how residential status decides which income is taxed in India.
Add back disallowances, swap book depreciation for tax depreciation, and explain each difference with a number.
Classify, check threshold and PAN, deduct, deposit, file the quarterly return, issue the certificate; and what a missed deduction costs.
15%, 45%, 75% and 100% by 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March, and interest when short.
Books first, portal second: match income and tax credits, and explain every gap.
Who needs one and what is reported: Forms 3CA/3CB with 3CD for FY 2025–26, the combined Form 26 from tax year 2026–27.
Who can opt for it, how income is worked out, and when books must still be kept.
Expenses allowed only on payment (statutory dues, MSME dues), cash payment limits, and expenses where TDS was missed.
Original, belated, revised and updated returns, and which ITR form suits which taxpayer.
Intimation vs scrutiny, the papers you collect, and how a reply is put together.
Is it a supply? Intra- or inter-state? Rate, time and value? Credit? Ask in that order.
What counts as a supply, and how composite and mixed supplies are taxed, with one example each.
CGST with SGST or IGST from the place of supply; when tax falls due on goods, services and advances.
The conditions, blocked credits with examples, and no credit on the tax portion where depreciation is claimed on it.
Credit claimed should match 2B. In IMS you accept, reject or keep invoices pending, and 2B can be recomputed before 3B is filed.
Read it from the notification, not the ledger name; the common services; the entry and the credit.
What each return reports, and how they tie to the books and to each other every month.
Books vs GSTR-1, 3B vs 1, books vs 2B, and turnover vs the financial statements; explain each difference.
Two main rates, 5% and 18%, and 40% for a short list of luxury and demerit goods.
When registration is needed, one PAN with a GSTIN in each state, and who can opt for composition.
Exports and SEZ supplies are zero-rated and keep their credit; exempt supplies need the related credit reversed.
What each document is for and when it applies.

topics.topic: What an article does in a branch audit
topics.know: Advances, drawing power, asset classification, KYC and documentation, and the reports the branch auditor signs.
When an account turns non-performing, and the special-mention stages that warn of it first.
Stock and debtors less the margin, and what you report when the outstanding is above it.
A year-end opinion vs a running check of the branch's daily transactions.
Character, capacity, capital, collateral and conditions; interest cover and debt service.
What a sanctioned loan file must hold, and the gaps an auditor looks for.
Prices between related companies across borders must be at arm's length, so profit isn't shifted out of India.
CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split and other method, and why TNMM is used most.
Screen comparables, compute their margins, and test where the client's margin falls.
Functions, assets and risks decide which entity should earn what.
The records kept every year and the accountant's report filed with the return.
TP interviews still ask TDS, heads of income and the new Act. Keep your Core tax ready.

topics.topic: What an M&A tax team does
topics.know: Tax on deals: structuring, tax due diligence and the compliance that follows a deal.
Short vs long term, cost and holding period, and how a sale of shares is taxed.
What each one is, and the tax question each one raises, in outline.
Three ways to return cash to shareholders, and the tax angle of each, in outline.
Why a buyer checks TDS before paying for shares or a business, above all to a non-resident seller.
One line each: tax treaties, permanent establishment and the tax residency certificate.
Income, market and cost (asset) approaches, and when each one fits.
The bridge between them: net debt and debt-like items.
Free cash flows, discount rate, terminal value, enterprise value, then equity value.
Cost of equity from CAPM, post-tax cost of debt, weights at market value.
Perpetual growth vs exit multiple, and why it is often most of the value.
EV/EBITDA and P/E, and how you pick comparable companies.
The buyer's view and quality of earnings, not an opinion on the accounts.
One-off items, owner costs and related-party pricing: what you adjust and why.
The trend, the seasonality, and the normal level a buyer expects at closing.
Borrowings less cash, plus items such as overdue statutory dues and deferred payments.
Revenue up while cash falls, large year-end entries, reliance on related parties.
Monthly analyses of the P&L, balance sheet and cash on which a diligence report is built.
Looking into a specific wrong, with evidence fit for a dispute, vs an opinion on the accounts.
Pressure, opportunity and rationalisation, and the main families of fraud.
Duplicates, round sums, weekend entries, a vendor sharing an employee's bank account or address.
The first-digit pattern and how it helps pick entries to test.
No or mismatched GSTIN, no real address or website, payments just under approval limits.
Keep the chain of evidence, record facts, never accuse, and tell only those who need to know.
Internal audit, IFC, process reviews and risk assessments for clients.
Explain any business process this way. It is the core of the work.
Types of controls, maker-checker, and how you test one control.
Profit is price times volume less costs. Ask questions, split the problem, give one recommendation.
Split a problem into parts that don't overlap, and say your structure before your answer.
Clean data, one PivotTable, and one slide that says what it shows.
Journals, trial balance, Schedule III statements, bank reconciliation: the month-end order.
Accruals, prepayments, provisions, depreciation, and the GST and TDS entries.
Bank, vendor, customer and GST: why balances differ and how each item clears.
Monthly P&L against budget, variances explained, a one-page summary for management.
Board and general meetings, minutes, statutory registers and the annual filings, in outline.
Vouchers, ledgers and reports. Say only what you have really used.

topics.topic: What an article does in IB or research
topics.know: Company profiles, comparable companies, models and pitch material.
Walk through a DCF, and say when you would use EV/EBITDA or P/E.
The bridge between them, and why EV/EBITDA uses one and P/E the other.
Cash flow, debt service and working capital explain why a company with profits can still fail.
Indices, the market's P/E, and fundamental vs technical analysis.
Business, numbers, peers and a view. Practise on one listed company before the interview.
Grammar, error spotting, vocabulary, sentence order, a short passage, and picking the right professional email.
Percentages, profit and discount, interest, ratios, averages, time and work, speed and distance, data from a table.
Series, coding, syllogisms, seating grids, directions, family relations, data sufficiency.
Pick the best first action, not the most heroic one.
Inter-level one-liners, plus one business-awareness question.
Do the easy ones first. With negative marking, guess only after you rule out options.
Owning an error, asking a client for documents, a fee revision; and an 80–120-word view on a current topic.
Repeat a sentence, read aloud, build a sentence, answer briefly. Work on clarity and pace, not accent.
Content, listening, bringing others in and a fair summary. Not the loudest voice.
Practise it on one abstract topic, one case and one current-affairs topic.
Five ways to open, and how to sum up both sides in the last minute.
Link to the last point, add one new idea, disagree with the point and never the person.
15 minutes a day for the month before. Five things to explain: Budget headlines, RBI's stance, a GST Council decision, the new Income-tax Act, one corporate story.
Camera on, muted until you speak, enter at a pause, no notes on screen.
Six to eight on a call: opener, regulator, summariser, observer. Two rounds, one fix each.

steps: Your three 'why' answers: CA, this firm, this domain.
Your favourite standards with their disclosures.
One fresh fact about the firm and the team.
Clothes, two printed CVs, mark sheets and ID laid out.

testWeek.title: A written test this week?
steps: Days 7 to 4: one timed mixed paper a day; note your weak sections.
Days 3 and 2: only the weak sections, Core basics and the last three months' business news.
Day before: light revision of formulas; laptop, internet, camera and ID checked.
Test day: join 15 minutes early, read every instruction, start with what is easy.

items.check: Attempt months and CA Final eligibility on the tip of your tongue
Two printed copies of your CV
items.why: In colour if your CV uses colour.

items.check: A pen and a small notebook
Phone on silent, water, washroom before you go in
items.why: Rounds can run back to back for hours.

items.check: Meet, Teams and Zoom tested a day before
items.why: Camera, mic, mute and screen share in each.

items.check: Quiet room, desk clear, no notes on screen
items.why: You may be asked to show the room.

items.check: Plain wall behind, light on your face, camera at eye level
Phone hotspot and charger as backup
Formal clothes in full, not only on top

notes.title: If the call drops
notes.text: Say calmly what happened, offer to rejoin or reschedule, then send a two-line mail.

notes.title: Walk in like this
notes.text: Smile. A small town or a small firm is one confident line, never an apology.

notes.title: After
notes.text: A thank-you mail the same day. Then log the questions in My interviews.
